claims.claim: Disparate impact liability under Title VII is statutory — recognised in Griggs v. Duke Power Co. (1971) and codified by Congress in the Civil Rights Act of 1991
claims.canonicalWording: Always pair the codification with the point that an executive order cannot repeal a statute. The two facts are only useful together.

claims.claim: EO 14281 (April 2025) directs federal agencies to eliminate disparate impact liability from civil rights enforcement
The EEOC dropped pending disparate impact cases, and in June 2026 issued a National Enforcement Plan prioritising disparate treatment theories over disparate impact theories

EO 14398, 'Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors', signed 26 March 2026 — flow-down clause to subcontractors, 'reasonably knowable' disclosure duty, books-and-records access, enforcement including False Claims Act actions

cautions: The posture is contested in both directions and litigation challenging these orders is live. State direction of travel, never a settled position.

The load-bearing teaching point is that enforcement retreat is not exposure reduction — it relocates exposure to the private plaintiffs' bar. A module that reports the retreat without that point teaches the opposite of what is intended.
